<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-benchmark-docs.mjs. Edit the script, not this file. -->

How `@cookiemonsterdev/kafka-core` compares with `@platformatic/kafka`, `kafkajs` and `@confluentinc/kafka-javascript` on Node.js 24, Node.js 26 and Bun. The headline workload sends 1 KiB values with a key and headers. A second workload with 100 B values is a stress test of per-record client overhead. Each table shows both side by side.

## Read this first

- The 100 B results stress per-record client overhead: with little data per record, they rank clients mostly by the work each does per record. The 1 KiB results are the headline.
- Only kafka-core verifies record-batch CRCs while consuming, so it does extra work in the consume and latency results.
- Concurrent sends favour clients that merge separate `send()` calls into one batch, as kafka-core does. Batched send is the fairer produce comparison.
- Confluent's client runs on Node.js 24 only. Its consume runs can run out of memory under the 2 GiB limit: a median covers the runs that finished, and a cell where every run failed has no value.
- All results come from one machine. Treat small differences as inconclusive.
- A chart names the highest or lowest client on a runtime only when that client's runs separate from each other client's beyond noise: the runs of both are steady, their min–max ranges do not overlap, and their medians differ by more than the measured noise. Otherwise it says there is no clear highest or lowest. The [comparison rule](https://github.com/cookieMonsterDev/kafka/blob/develop/benchmarks/README.md#comparison-rule) has the details.

## Setup

### Payloads

| Payload | Role                            | Key  | Value   | Headers        |
| ------- | ------------------------------- | ---- | ------- | -------------- |
| 1 KiB   | Headline                        | 16 B | 1,024 B | 2, 16 B values |
| 100 B   | Per-record overhead stress test | 16 B | 100 B   | none           |

Records come from a fixed seed, so every client sends the same bytes in every session. Produce scenarios send the key, value and headers. Consume topics are seeded by Kafka's own `kafka-producer-perf-test.sh` with values only. The first record of each pool:

```text
1 KiB payload
  key:     oaiAFEM45BqQZohS
  value:   nllFj3ggk3mU784jQBEVmfvfoz3jIThm… (1,024 bytes)
  headers: h0=vQxYM0LwifDiUhLJ, h1=CWvHUVtzHWRmW1r0

100 B payload
  key:     oaiAFEM45BqQZohS
  value:   nllFj3ggk3mU784jQBEVmfvfoz3jIThm… (100 bytes)
  headers: none
```

### Record counts

Each run sends or reads its warm-up records first and measures only the rest. Measured time is the median time of the fastest and of the slowest client and runtime under the normalized profile; E1 instead runs for its fixed duration, and L1 times one record from process start. Every run gets a fresh topic with 3 partitions, deleted before the next run starts.

| Scenario                  | 1 KiB measured records | 1 KiB warm-up | 1 KiB measured time | 100 B measured records | 100 B warm-up | 100 B measured time |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------- | ------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------- | ------------------- |
| P1 `produce-single`       | 7,500                  | 500           | 0.6–0.8 s           | 30,000                 | 2,000         | 2.1–3.1 s           |
| P2 `produce-batch`        | 1,200,000              | 60,000        | 2.2–11.0 s          | 500,000                | 20,000        | 0.6–2.6 s           |
| P3 `produce-throughput`   | 250,000                | 12,500        | 0.7–12.5 s          | 1,000,000              | 50,000        | 1.9–46.8 s          |
| C1 `consume-each-message` | 500,000                | 12,500        | 0.3–4.3 s           | 2,000,000              | 50,000        | 0.5–1.9 s           |
| C2 `consume-each-batch`   | 500,000                | 12,500        | 0.3–3.4 s           | 2,000,000              | 50,000        | 0.4–1.1 s           |
| E1 `e2e-latency`          | 5,000/s for 15 s       | 5,000         | —                   | 5,000/s for 15 s       | 5,000         | —                   |
| L1 `startup`              | 1                      | 0             | —                   | 1                      | 0             | —                   |

### Wire settings

The normalized profile pins these settings for every client; each adapter maps them to its own options. The library-defaults chart sets only brokers, client id and group id.

| Scenario                | Produce calls                                   | Acks | Linger | Batch size | Max in-flight | Compression | Idempotent |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ---- | ------ | ---------- | ------------- | ----------- | ---------- |
| P1 `produce-single`     | sequential `send()` of 1 record                 | 1    | 0 ms   | 16 KiB     | 5             | none        | no         |
| P2 `produce-batch`      | sequential `send()` of 100 records              | 1    | 0 ms   | 16 KiB     | 5             | none        | no         |
| P3 `produce-throughput` | up to 256 concurrent `send()` calls of 1 record | 1    | 5 ms   | 16 KiB     | 5             | none        | no         |
| E1 `e2e-latency`        | one record per `send()` at a fixed rate         | 1    | 0 ms   | 16 KiB     | 5             | none        | no         |
| L1 `startup`            | one record                                      | 1    | 0 ms   | 16 KiB     | 5             | none        | no         |

| Scenario                  | Consume handler | Fetch min | Fetch max | Partition fetch max | Fetch max wait |
| ------------------------- | --------------- | --------- | --------- | ------------------- | -------------- |
| C1 `consume-each-message` | per record      | 1 B       | 50 MiB    | 1 MiB               | 100 ms         |
| C2 `consume-each-batch`   | batch           | 1 B       | 50 MiB    | 1 MiB               | 100 ms         |
| E1 `e2e-latency`          | per record      | 1 B       | 50 MiB    | 1 MiB               | 100 ms         |
| L1 `startup`              | per record      | 1 B       | 50 MiB    | 1 MiB               | 100 ms         |

### Environment

Every container runs on one Docker VM, each pinned to its own CPUs. Scenarios, fairness rules and the option mapping of each client are in the [benchmarks README](https://github.com/cookieMonsterDev/kafka/blob/develop/benchmarks/README.md).

| Setting          | 1 KiB                                                                                                   | 100 B                                                                                                   |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Session          | `20261116123949-ba6f0ab417cf`, standard tier, count scale 1                                             | `20261113170453-7a9308c82c8d`, standard tier, count scale 1                                             |
| Date             | 2026-11-16                                                                                              | 2026-11-13                                                                                              |
| Repetitions      | 5, interleaved                                                                                          | 5, interleaved                                                                                          |
| Clients          | kafka-core 2.8.1 (`ba6f0ab417cf`), Platformatic 2.15.0, KafkaJS 2.2.4 and Confluent 1.11.0              | kafka-core 2.7.0 (`7a9308c82c8d`), Platformatic 2.15.0, KafkaJS 2.2.4 and Confluent 1.11.0              |
| Runtimes         | Node.js 24.22.3, Node.js 26.13.1 and Bun 1.4.4                                                          | Node.js 24.22.3, Node.js 26.13.1 and Bun 1.4.4                                                          |
| Host             | Apple M5, 10 CPUs, 32 GiB, darwin 27.2.0 arm64                                                          | Apple M5, 10 CPUs, 32 GiB, darwin 27.2.0 arm64                                                          |
| Docker VM        | Docker 29.9.2, 6 vCPUs, 9.7 GiB                                                                         | Docker 29.9.2, 6 vCPUs, 9.7 GiB                                                                         |
| Broker           | `apache/kafka:4.3.2`, one KRaft node; 3 vCPUs (cpuset `0-2`), 5 GiB memory, 2 GiB heap, 2 GiB tmpfs log | `apache/kafka:4.3.2`, one KRaft node; 3 vCPUs (cpuset `0-2`), 5 GiB memory, 2 GiB heap, 2 GiB tmpfs log |
| Client container | 2 vCPUs (cpuset `3-4`), 2 GiB memory, swap off; a fresh container per run                               | 2 vCPUs (cpuset `3-4`), 2 GiB memory, swap off; a fresh container per run                               |

## Install size

What installing each client adds, measured in the benchmark image. Required is the package and everything it reaches through `dependencies`; optional is what its `optionalDependencies` add, which npm and pnpm skip when they cannot be installed.

This is information, not a ranking, because size follows what each client implements and bundles: kafka-core implements KIP-848 consumer groups, KIP-932 share groups and transactions (see [Compatibility](../compatibility/)), Platformatic and Confluent's client implement KIP-848 and transactions but not share groups, KafkaJS implements transactions but neither KIP-848 nor share groups, and Confluent's client bundles librdkafka as a native addon.

| Client       | Version | Required (MB) | Required dependencies | Required files | Optional (MB) | Optional dependencies | Optional files | Native addon  |
| ------------ | ------- | ------------- | --------------------- | -------------- | ------------- | --------------------- | -------------- | ------------- |
| kafka-core   | 2.8.1   | 2.16          | 3                     | 891            | 0.54          | 2                     | 9              | optional only |
| Platformatic | 2.15.0  | 4.62          | 16                    | 1,797          | 4.46          | 4                     | 129            | optional only |
| KafkaJS      | 2.2.4   | 0.73          | 0                     | 391            | 0.00          | 0                     | 0              | no            |
| Confluent    | 1.11.0  | 47.23         | 25                    | 1,316          | 0.00          | 0                     | 0              | yes           |

MB is 1,000,000 bytes.

## How to reproduce

From the repository root, with Docker running, run one session per payload. Regenerating the page from a session replaces only the results of its payload. A seed repeats the run order of the published session; record counts come from the current runner, so they can differ from the published ones listed under [Record counts](#record-counts).

### 1 KiB values

```sh
pnpm benchmarks:run --tier standard --payload medium --seed 3167347498
pnpm docs:benchmarks --competitors benchmarks/results/raw/<session> --core benchmarks/results/raw/<session>
```

### 100 B values

```sh
pnpm benchmarks:run --tier standard --payload small --seed 4214559388
pnpm docs:benchmarks --competitors benchmarks/results/raw/<session> --core benchmarks/results/raw/<session>
```

### Results from other hardware

Results hold as ratios on the machine that produced them. To contribute results from another machine, run `pnpm benchmarks:doctor` and fix what it reports, run both sessions above, then [open an issue](https://github.com/cookieMonsterDev/kafka/issues/new/choose) with each session's `summary.json` and `report.md` from `benchmarks/results/raw/<session>/`. Do not edit this page: it is generated.
